finding.claim: The /admin/users/<uid>/ban handler calls do_ban(uid) even when the admin check fails. require_admin's abort(403) is caught by the surrounding except Exception, so a non-admin POST reaches the privileged ban action and receives 200 {ok: true}.
finding.source: Any HTTP POST to /admin/users/<uid>/ban by a caller whose g.user lacks is_admin. The uid path parameter is attacker-controlled.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the privileged account-ban operation. It is a stub in this file; the real implementation is not in the repo.

trace.note: Route registered for POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban; no before_request or decorator enforces admin in this file
require_admin(g.user) is called inside a try block
For a non-admin user, abort(403) is reached at line 11 and raises a werkzeug HTTPException
except Exception catches the HTTPException, since HTTPException subclasses Exception, so the 403 never reaches the client
Only log.warning is emitted; execution continues
Returns jsonify(ok=True) to the non-admin caller

finding.guards_checked: (1) require_admin's abort(403) is defeated because the broad except at line 18 swallows it. (2) No route-level decorator or before_request admin check exists in admin.py. (3) The unban route (lines 24-28) does not have this bug because its check is not wrapped, so the issue is specific to ban. Not verified: where g.user is populated (auth middleware is not in the repo), and whether do_ban is protected elsewhere (its body is pass here). Matches case 01 (perm-result-ignored); no decoy applies.

verdict.guard_found: admin.py:10-11 require_admin raises abort(403), but its result is only reached inside a try whose bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18-19 swallows the HTTPException and only logs a warning, so execution continues to do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20. No route decorator or before_request admin check exists in admin.py. The unban route (admin.py:26) calls require_admin outside any try and is not affected. Auth middleware that sets g.user is not in the repo.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: require_admin's abort(403) at admin.py:11 is caught by the broad except at admin.py:18, and do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs unconditionally before jsonify(ok=True) at admin.py:21. Any authenticated caller whose g.user lacks is_admin can therefore reach the ban action, and nothing in this repo blocks it, though an external before_request that the repo does not contain could still enforce admin.
